requested.title: Client half of the isomorphic `cookies` API silently drops the app's `cookie:defaults` (Secure / SameSite / path)
Request-context proxies have no `set` trap, so assignments silently write to a dead target and vanish
Analytics tracker injected on token-bearing URLs leaks newsletter confirm/unsubscribe tokens to a third party
First-occurrence String.replace on fully-rendered HTML lets page content hijack the analytics injection point
Attacker-chosen dimensions on an unauthenticated, synchronous, un-memoized server-side rasterizer stall the whole event loop
Unauthenticated always-throwing routes emit two full stack traces per request with no rate limit

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Every mechanical claim verified. `packages/mochi/src/runtime/cookies.client.ts:20` is exactly `Cookies.set(name, value, options ? { ...options } : undefined)` — only per-call options are forwarded. The server half at `cookies.ts:99` does `serializeCookie(name, value, { ...this.defaults, ...options })`, with `this.defaults` coming from `applyFilter('cookie:defaults', {}, { options })` at `Mochi.ts:494`. I traced `cookieDefaults` through every reference in the framework (Mochi.ts:735/776/1848/1899, requestSetup.ts:128, errors.ts:54) and it is only ever fed into a `MochiCookieJar` constructor — it is never serialized into the page, unlike `window.__mochi_log_level` (Mochi.ts:315), so the client genuinely cannot see it. The vendored js-cookie's sole default is `init(defaultConverter, { path: '/' })` (vendor/js-cookie/index.ts:154), and `remove()` delegates to `set()`, which merges `defaultAttributes` first — so a client-side `cookies.delete('x')` always writes `Path=/`. The doc contract is broken as cited: `162-extensions.md:152` says the defaults are merged into *every* `cookies.set()` call with no server-only caveat, and `85-request-context.md:66,109` present cookies as one isomorphic API; `mochi-framework.d.ts:35-39` likewise types a single `CookieJar`. The most demonstrable consequence is functional, not cryptographic: with a configured `path: '/app'`, a server `set` emits `Path=/app` while a client `delete` emits a `Path=/` expiry that cannot match, so the cookie survives, and a client `set` creates a second same-name cookie scoped to `/`. The security consequence (a centrally-enforced `secure: true` silently absent on island-written cookies) is real but conditional — it needs a downstream app to opt into the filter AND a plaintext path to the host; `httpOnly` is inherently impossible from `document.cookie` and `sameSite` is largely absorbed by Lax-by-default. No workspace in this repo configures `cookie:defaults` (only `extensions.test.ts` does), so the exposure is to downstream `mochi-framework` consumers rather than mochi.fast. Keeping MEDIUM: a published framework silently voiding a security attribute it documents as universal warrants a security label even though the window is narrow.

Confirmed by spec-level trace. `__mochiCtxProxy` (mochi-env.server.js:9-23) builds `new Proxy({}, …)` with `get`/`has`/`ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps that all forward to `getRequestContext()[key]`; the target is never read. With no `set` trap, `proxy.p = v` runs OrdinarySet on the throwaway `{}`: ownDesc is undefined, so it walks to `Object.prototype`, lands on a default writable descriptor, then does `CreateDataProperty(Receiver=proxy, …)` → no `defineProperty` trap → the value is written to the dummy. The next read goes through `get` to the real context and returns the old/undefined value. Write silently lost, confirmed. Reachability is narrower than the finding implies in one way and broader in another: `index.ts` does NOT export `locals`/`params`/`url`/`cookies` at all (I enumerated its exports), so these bindings exist only inside compiled code — but `registerMochiEnvClient`/the server equivalent resolve bare `mochi-framework` for every module in the bundle graph, so `.svelte`, `.svelte.ts` and plain `.ts` files in that graph are all affected. `mochi-framework.d.ts:51` types `locals` as a mutable `Record<string, unknown>` (vs. `params`'s `Readonly<…>`), so a component write type-checks and fails only at runtime, which is precisely the silent-failure shape described. The client `url` proxy's `set() { return false }` (mochi-env.client.js:30) corroborates the omission. One consequence the finding missed strengthens it: when the real context already owns the key, OrdinarySet takes the `existingDescriptor` branch and calls `Reflect.defineProperty(target, p, { value })`, creating a **non-configurable** property on the module-lifetime dummy. On a later request where the context lacks that key, the `ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps then violate proxy invariants and throw a `TypeError` on `Object.keys(locals)`, `{...locals}` or `Object.entries(locals)` — cross-request state pollution in a long-lived process. BUG severity is correct; this is a correctness defect, not a security boundary.

The whole chain holds. `analytics()` installs a `transformPage` that fills `{{mochi.analytics}}` on every `text/html` response; `packages/support/src/index.ts:41` mounts it site-wide as `sequence(adminAuth, embedHeaders, analytics({ exclude: [NEWSLETTER_EMBED_PATH] }))` and `support/src/shell.html:123` carries the placeholder. `NEWSLETTER_EMBED_PATH` is only `/newsletter/embed` (embedHeaders.ts:4), while `newsletter/routes.ts:84` and `:106` define `/newsletter/confirm` and `/newsletter/unsubscribe` as `Mochi.page` routes whose sole authorization is `url.searchParams.get('token')` — the route comment says so outright. `stripTrailingSlash('/newsletter/confirm/')` yields `/newsletter/confirm`, which is not in the exclude Set, so `enabled` is true. Tokens are `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')` (db.server.ts:251) placed in the query string by `confirmUrl`/`unsubscribeUrl` (newsletter/config.ts). `analyticsTracker.html` sets only `data-website-id` and `data-performance`; I confirmed via Umami's documentation that `data-exclude-search` defaults to off, i.e. the tracker reports `pathname + search` and the token lands in the analytics store. Production reach is confirmed: `Dockerfile.production:75` sets `ENV MOCHI_DOCKER=true`, and `.github/workflows/build.yml:67-72` builds the `support` workspace from `Dockerfile.production` and deploys it as `mochi-support`/support.mochi.fast. No CSP constrains script-src (embedHeaders only sets `frame-ancestors`, and only on the embed path). Two honest mitigations the finding understates: `u.khromov.se` is the project owner's own self-hosted Umami, so 'third party' is really 'third-party-hosted script plus token sprawl into analytics storage'; and the worst outcome is an unauthorized newsletter confirm (defeating double opt-in) or unsubscribe, not account compromise. The unsubscribe token never expires, though, and tokens persist in analytics far beyond `CONFIRM_TTL_MS`. The closing remark about `/newsletter/%65mbed/` is speculative (an undecoded pathname likely fails to route at all) but immaterial. MEDIUM stands for a live production bearer-credential-in-URL leak.

Not a duplicate of F3: F3 is about *where* the tracker is enabled (missing exclusions / query-string reporting), F4 is about *how* the substitution is performed — different root cause, different fix. The premise verified: `applyResolveOptions` (runtime/hooks.ts:170-183) is the only call site, it does `await result.text()` on the finished Response and passes that to `opts.transformPage` with `done: true`, so `{{mochi.body}}` is already replaced with rendered component output. `html.replace('{{mochi.analytics}}', …)` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence, and both shells place the placeholder at the very end of `<body>` (support:123, site:415), after all content — so any earlier occurrence wins. The attacker path is real: the unauthenticated `send` action (support/src/routes.ts) stores `message` after only whitespace-trim and a 5000-char slice, and `admin/SubmissionCard.svelte:23` renders `{submission.message}` in a text position where Svelte SSR escaping touches only `&` and `<` — `{{mochi.analytics}}` contains neither, so it reaches `transformPage` byte-identical and the tracker `<script>` is injected into the message paragraph while the real placeholder renders as literal text. I also found a publicly reachable variant the finding didn't name: `/newsletter/embed`'s `source` prop comes from `?src=` (newsletter/routes.ts:25) and lands in `NewsletterForm.svelte:64` as `value={source}` inside a double-quoted attribute; that path is excluded so `enabled` is false, meaning a crafted `?src={{mochi.analytics}}` swallows the empty-string replacement and leaves the real placeholder visible — same hijack, no auth needed. I confirmed the finding's own caveats: `ANALYTICS_SCRIPT` contains no `"` (only single quotes), so it cannot break out of a Svelte-emitted double-quoted attribute, and it contains no `$`, so the `$&`/`` $` `` replacement-pattern hazard is latent rather than live. So this is a robustness/correctness defect with attacker-controlled trigger and cosmetic impact today, exactly as filed — the fragility argument (the documented `%nonce%` variant at `150-custom-html-shell.md:71` would be a CSP break) is sound. BUG severity is correct.

Verified end to end. The route is mounted (`packages/site/src/routes.ts:28,355`), is a bare `Mochi.api` with no auth, and `protection.protect` in site/src/index.ts:191 matches only `/demos/protection*`; there is no server-wide `rateLimit` in `Mochi.serve()`. `clampSize` admits [64, 2000], so 2000x2000 = 4,000,000 px against the demo page's own `` (Charts.svelte:200) = 153,600 px — a 26x pixel amplification, and the inline comment at line 7 addresses only memory. The synchrony claim is correct: `node_modules/layerchart/dist/server/index.js` `renderChart` calls `render()`, forces `void rendered.body`, then `renderCapturedChart` → `createCanvas` → `renderTree(ctx, …)` → `canvas.toBuffer(mimeType)` with no `await` anywhere, and `serverChart.ts` types it `=> Uint8Array`. On Bun's single JS thread that blocks everything. No server-side memoization exists — only the `Bun.build` bundle is cached in `bundle`; bytes are re-rendered every call. `noCache` leaves the route's `public, max-age=3600` intact (it early-returns when `cache-control` is already set), but an extra random query param busts any shared cache. Crucially, I confirmed the bypass is structural rather than requiring spoofing: the limiter keys on `getClientAddress() ?? 'unknown'` (rateLimit.ts:~250) and site/src/index.ts:201 sets `proxy: { addressHeader: 'x-forwarded-for', xffDepth: 1 }`, so the key is each visitor's real IP — a distributed `` on an attacker page gives every visitor a fresh 60/min quota. On magnitude I'd temper the finding slightly: cost is dominated by PNG-encoding a mostly-flat 4 Mpx canvas, order 10²ms rather than seconds, so one IP alone buys a fraction of a core and sustained saturation needs the distributed variant. The `src/demos/*` known-false-positive carve-out does not cover this: it is about auth/secrets demo patterns (hardcoded `hunter2`, no auth), and commit 1289d8f8 ('bound unbounded resource growth on public demo routes') shows resource exhaustion on exactly this file is treated as a product concern. MEDIUM stands as residual risk after that hardening.

Every mechanical claim checks out. `Error500.svelte` is three lines and its `<script>` throws unconditionally, so both `/demos/error/500` and `/demos/error/redirect` fail on every SSR render; neither declares `rateLimit`, and site/src/index.ts has no server-wide limit. I traced the logging precisely through `runtime/errors.ts`: `renderErrorResponseInner` invokes `handleError` at line 69, which emits `logger.info('handleError: …')` (index.ts:49) and `logger.error('app:', pathname, error)` (index.ts:53, since `error && status >= 500`), then returns `undefined` because the redirect branch tests `'/demos/error/redirect/'`; control reaches line 89-91 and the framework logs the 5xx with the thrown error a second time. `logger: { level: 'log' }` is level 4, above both `error` (1) and `info` (3), so all three lines print — one info line plus two full stack traces, exactly as claimed. The finding is careful to attribute the doubling only to `/demos/error/500/`, which is right: for `/demos/error/redirect/` the hook returns a Response and line 75 returns before the framework's log, so that route emits one trace. The error page is also uncached (`noCache` sets `Cache-Control: no-cache` on the `page`-kind response, which has none). So the duplicate-logging defect is genuine and the comment at errors.ts:87-88 confirms the framework deliberately logs after the hook, making the app's own `logger.error` redundant. I'm downgrading MEDIUM to BUG because the DoS framing is thin: amplification is ~30-70x in log bytes, the attacker's achievable rate is bounded by the full error-page SSR the server performs for any page, and the disk-exhaustion endpoint depends on an unrotated Docker json-file driver — an ops configuration gap, not a code defect. The durable, actionable content here is the redundant 5xx log plus the absence of a bound on deliberately-throwing public routes.
